LESSON: CITIZENSHIP

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Developments and Governance
Topic 5.3: Citizenship

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Citizenship. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we promote global citizenship?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe qualities of a global citizen in an interconnected society
2. explain factors for harmonious coexistence among citizens in East Africa and Africa

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CITIZENSHIP
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Citizenship helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: CITIZENSHIP
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Describe qualities of a global citizen in an interconnected society

What this means
In this part you learn to describe qualities of a global citizen in an interconnected society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe qualities of a global citizen in an interconnected society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Citizenship” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe qualities of a global citizen in an interconnected society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain factors for harmonious coexistence among citizens in East Africa and Africa

What this means
In this part you learn to explain factors for harmonious coexistence among citizens in East Africa and Africa. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain factors for harmonious coexistence among citizens in East Africa and Africa.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Citizenship.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain factors for harmonious coexistence among citizens in East Africa and Africa. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Citizenship is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Citizenship” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: describe qualities of a global citizen in an interconnected society)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Citizenship. (skill: explain factors for harmonious coexistence among citizens in East Africa and Africa)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Citizenship to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe qualities of a global citizen in an interconnected society.
3. Practise this skill: explain factors for harmonious coexistence among citizens in East Africa and Africa.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Citizenship from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Citizenship: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Citizenship?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we promote global citizenship?
2. How can we show empathy as global citizens?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Citizenship means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe qualities of a global citizen in an interconnected society.
5. Be able to: explain factors for harmonious coexistence among citizens in East Africa and Africa.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
